title: continuous learned depth address
hypothesis: A compact polynomial depth address driving a shared Givens view can recover unobserved intermediate layer functions from endpoint and sparse-depth supervision, at lower serialized bytes than independent layers and better held-out quality than tying, static step LoRA, and generated diagonal modulation.
physical_object: One shared 8x8 linear block reused at eight logical depths
mirror_coordinate: Normalized depth address [z,z^2] mapped to one learned Givens angle
logical_multiplicity: Eight depth-specific maps, with only depths 0,2,5,7 supervised during training

development.selection_metric: held-out intermediate-depth test MSE after 600 Adam updates at LR 0.01

success_gate: For the aligned teacher, Mirror held-out-depth MSE <=1.10x the best among tied and generated-address controls and <=1.10x the all-depth untied oracle in 3/3 fresh worlds; payload <=0.80x untied. Report independent teacher as boundary. This remains a fixed-budget interpolation/learning-efficiency screen.
failure_gate: On both development worlds, Mirror held-out MSE is >1.10x the best generalizing simple control, or the aligned quality/byte gate is missed. Do not open fresh worlds after failure.
boundaries: Only four of eight depths supervised
Normalized polynomial address fixed in advance
CPU screen; not a capacity or language claim
